sentences: Subgraph-freeness asks whether a network avoids a fixed graph H while communicating through bounded-size messages.
The source asks whether any two-connected H admits a subpolynomial-round algorithm, or whether every such target forces a polynomial lower bound.
Two-connectivity isolates patterns whose cycles cannot be separated by deleting a single vertex.
The paper's reductions would turn hardness for all these patterns into a broad distinction between trees and connected graphs containing cycles.
Resolving the question would therefore organize many individual detection bounds into a structural explanation of when local patterns require substantial global communication.
